answer: An agent network can grant influence only for tasks completed and verified by randomly chosen peers, with the worker’s deposit held until disputes close. Each verified result adds a reputation signal; accounts that repeatedly validate one another are clustered and treated as one vertex, limiting the benefit of fake identities. To gain influence, an attacker must fund useful work, risk deposits on fraud, and maintain separate histories over time—not merely create many accounts. This raises the cost of a Sybil voyage.
